title: CDMO water systems: client-auditable PW and WFI | Aquemi
meta: PW and WFI for CDMOs, built to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute, with Part 11 trend data and an audit pack every client can follow.
eyebrow: CONTRACT MANUFACTURING · CDMO · MULTI-CLIENT, MULTI-MARKET · USP AND PH. EUR. · 21 CFR PART 11
headline: One water system, audited by every client and every regulator they ship to
lead: A contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) does not get one water audit a year. It gets one per client, plus Health Canada, the FDA and EU or other PIC/S inspectors for the markets those clients sell into, and an outage stops several clients' batches at once. We design Purified Water (PW) and Water for Injection (WFI) systems to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute: USP <645> 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C, Ph. Eur. nitrates 0.2 ppm, 500 ppb total organic carbon (TOC) and, for WFI, < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin at the point of use. We build in the redundancy your client commitments need, and hand over the factory acceptance test (FAT) report, installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) records and trend data under 21 CFR Part 11 that any client auditor can follow without a guide.

blocks.h: In a CDMO, the water system is shared evidence
body: Every product on your site is made with the same water, so every client's quality unit reads the same records. One client audits against its US filing, the next against Ph. Eur. and its EU Qualified Person's checklist, a third sends a supplier questionnaire before it signs. Health Canada inspects the site under your drug establishment licence, and the FDA and EU or other PIC/S authorities inspect it when a client's product is filed in their market.

That changes what a good water system is. It has to meet the strictest market any client ships to, on every attribute, before the client asks. Its records have to be portable: a trend report, an excursion history or a change log you can send to one client without showing another client's data. It has to absorb a new programme on a tech transfer timeline you did not set. And it has to keep running, because a day without water is a day of missed batches across several contracts.

Your water system is also part of your sales pitch. When a prospective client's due diligence team asks what water you make, how you trend it and what happens when it fails, a clear answer helps win the programme. We design for that question from the user requirement specification (URS).

body: A client whose product is filed in Japan or another market may name a further pharmacopoeia. Send us the markets for each client programme and we map every attribute in the compliance matrix before design, so the strictest-of rule is a written decision, not an assumption.

Limits are as the pharmacopoeias state them (Ph. Eur. 0008 as revised in Ph. Eur. 12.3, in force 1 July 2026). Ph. Eur. adds aluminium ≤ 10 ppb and an endotoxin limit on PW only where it is used to make dialysis solutions. Alert and action levels for your site are set from qualification data.

blocks.h: Who audits your water system, and where we answer it
cols: What they read on the water system
rows: Health Canada, under your drug establishment licence

GUI-0001 on Part C, Division 2 of the Food and Drug Regulations: premises, equipment, sanitation, validation and records, including written agreements for contracted activities. For sterile work, GUI-0119, Health Canada's adoption of EU GMP Annex 1 (2022)
FDA, when a client's product is filed in the United States

21 CFR Part 211: equipment design (211.63), maintenance (211.67), automatic equipment and records (211.68), and electronic records to Part 11. A pre-approval inspection of your site for a client's application reads a full year of water data, as the FDA Guide to Inspections of High Purity Water Systems sets out
EU authorities and your clients' Qualified Persons

Ph. Eur. on every attribute, the EMA water guideline, Annex 15 qualification and EU GMP Chapter 7 on outsourced activities. The Canada–EU mutual recognition agreement (MRA) on GMP covers many drug products; your regulatory team confirms the scope for each client's product
Other PIC/S authorities, such as the MHRA, TGA or Swissmedic
The PIC/S GMP guide, which follows EU GMP, and PIC/S PI 041-1 on data integrity: complete, attributable records with audit trails that are reviewed
Your clients' quality units

The quality agreement: who owns the water system, what is reported to the client and how fast, change notification and audit rights, framed by ICH Q10 section 2.7 and the FDA guidance Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements (2016). Then trend reports, excursion investigations and the change log for their campaign
Prospective clients, in due diligence

Supplier questionnaires and site visits: water grades, capacity, sanitization method, online monitoring, alert and action levels, recent excursions. The answers decide whether your site makes the shortlist

blocks.h: How the systems connect in a multi-client plant
blocks.caption: Duplex RO and EDI trains make PW into storage and one or more loops, with valved tie-ins for future suites. Sterile and biologics suites take WFI from a still or a membrane skid, and pure steam for autoclaves and SIP. Each loop and suite has its own sample points and online instruments, mapped by tag number. Monitoring and controls run across all of it, with audit-trailed records under 21 CFR Part 11 that report by suite and point of use.

blocks.h: Decisions to settle before the URS is approved

items.t: Size for the pipeline, not only the current contracts
items.d: Generation, storage and loop sized from your signed programmes plus the ones your business development team expects, with spare skid space and valved tie-ins qualified with the original system.
The strictest market any client ships to sets each attribute. Writing that rule into the URS saves a requalification when a client files in a new market.
Separate loops for different suites or grades can confine an excursion to one client's area. One loop costs less. We compare them on your client mix and risk.

items.t: Reports by suite, from day one
items.d: Tag numbers, sample point names and report filters that follow your suites make the client audit pack an export. Adding them later means re-mapping a qualified system.
Membrane WFI costs less to run, but a client whose filing names distillation, or a market that requires notice, can decide for you. We list each client's constraint before choosing.

Feed temperature can swing from near freezing in winter to over 20 °C in summer, and some municipal supplies use chloramine. We size membranes at your coldest month and design chloramine removal ahead of the RO.

blocks.h: Questions CDMO engineering, validation and QA leads ask

items.q: Can one water system serve clients filing in Canada, the United States and Europe?
items.a: Yes. We design each attribute to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur., test both at FAT where the methods allow it and write the basis into the functional specification. The same records then answer Health Canada, the FDA, an EU Qualified Person and each client's auditor.

items.q: Who owns the water system data, us or our clients?
items.a: You do. The water system is a site utility. Your quality agreements set what each client receives, how fast and in what form. We build the reporting so you can give each client the data for its campaign and points of use without exposing anyone else's.

items.q: A new client starts tech transfer in a few months. Must the whole system be requalified?
items.a: Not normally. The change goes through your change control, and a risk assessment sets the scope: usually IQ and OQ for the new section and a period of increased sampling at the new points of use. We state that scope before design and plan the tie-in around your shutdown and your other clients' campaigns.

items.q: Is duplex generation worth the cost?
items.a: It depends on what a day without water costs you in missed batches across your contracts, and on how long your storage lasts with generation stopped. We put the capital cost of duplex or N+1 next to that figure in the proposal, so the decision is yours and on paper.

items.q: Can you attend our clients' audits?
items.a: [Confirm whether Aquemi attends client audits and regulatory inspections as the water system supplier, in person or by video, and on what terms: included in a service plan, or charged per day.]

items.q: Can you help us answer a prospective client's supplier questionnaire?
items.a: [Confirm whether Aquemi provides a water system capability sheet and supports questionnaire answers for CDMO business development, and whether a service plan includes it.]

items.q: Our system was built by someone else and our records are on paper. Where do we start?
items.a: With a system assessment: drawings against the plant, the qualification file, trend data and data integrity controls, checked against what your current clients and markets expect. You get a gap list ranked by audit risk, and the requalification scope for each fix.

items.a: [Number and type of CDMO or contract manufacturing references Aquemi can offer for a call; or a plain statement if none can be named yet.]
